experiment.question: How do agent latency, the Collectd thread count, CPU and RAM relate to each other, and is there a rule for sizing a deployment?
experiment.independent_variable: workload.parameters.devices, across six knee searches, a latency sweep and a cleanroom edge search
experiment.plan: No new measurement. Every knee the campaign recorded between 1 and 6 September 2026 on kfk-exclusive is read back from its own records (knee-search*.jsonl, edge-search.jsonl, latency-sweep.jsonl, fleet-sweep.jsonl, the sealed captures) by bin/model.py, which derives two constants per collection, thread time T = P x R + c0 and CPU cost c, and predicts each knee from them: threads x 300 / T by the pool, cores x utilisation x 300 / c by the processor, whichever is smaller. The figures are the searches' own Prometheus series, re-expressed in the rule's units.

sut.config_delta:
A synthesis across the campaign's configurations rather than one configuration. The Core VM was 16 GiB with a 10 GiB heap (JAVA_HEAP_SIZE 10240) until 2026-09-05 09:15Z and 32 GiB with a 20 GiB heap after (xxlarge-mem, commit f6a9609); 8 vCPU throughout, G1 throughout. Collectd threads 100 (latency sweep, edge search, cleanroom, first knee search), 200, 300 and 400 by search. snmp-config max-repetitions 2 (default) until 2026-09-04 11:57Z and 5 for 10.42.0.0/16 after, set through the Config Manager. netem on the simulator's SNMP interface: none and 0 to 60 ms in the latency sweep, delay 10ms 2ms in the edge search, none in the cleanroom, delay 75ms 25ms in every knee search. The Minion, Kafka, PostgreSQL and nl6 as in the sealed captures; the Kafka compression trials of 2026-09-06 evening are excluded.

Per-window sources: campaigns/pm-snmp-latency/results (latency-sweep, fleet-sweep, edge-search), experiments/pm-snmp-14k-cleanroom, campaigns/pm-snmp-agent-latency/results (knee-search*.jsonl, pool-sweep.jsonl), and the sealed captures pm-snmp-agent-latency-mr5-live, -32g-live and -32g-pool400-live.

answers.question: How do agent latency and PDUs per collection set the thread count?
What does a collection cost the processor, and does latency change it?
How much heap and RAM does a fleet need?
Does the rule reproduce every knee the campaign found?
How is a deployment sized with it, and in which order are the levers pulled?

gaps.question: Are the constants those of one device type?
gaps.why: Every fleet in the campaign is the same simulated Cisco CRS-X with 144 interfaces and the same data collection package: 1,738 samples per collection, 61 or 149 PDUs by max-repetitions. c0 and c are per-collection costs of that shape. A device with 48 interfaces or a package with fewer tables changes P, c0 and c together; the form of the rule does not change, its constants must be re-read.

gaps.question: Does a uniform netem delay stand for a real fleet's latency?
gaps.why: The latency sweep and every knee search delay every response by a fixed or uniform amount. Real agents answer some tables fast and others slowly, and slow ones time out; the rule's R is the mean round trip a collection experiences, which a real fleet needs measured from its own pcap or from the Collectd instrumentation log.

gaps.question: Is c0 a constant?
gaps.why: The Core-side second per collection is 0.5 s at low utilisation and rises towards 1 s above 90% CPU as the response handlers queue for cores; the rule uses 0.75 s. That is why thread time reads 5.4 to 5.6 s at the 32 GiB knees against the 5.1 s the constant predicts, and why the pool limit lands 5% high on the last rung before the processor binds.

gaps.question: Is CPU per collection the right cost measure?
gaps.why: It is CPU busy times cores over collections completed and includes everything else the Core does: provisiond rescans, the JMX exporter, logging, garbage collection. On the 16 GiB Core the GC share inflates it from 0.115 to 0.13 to 0.16; the rule uses the 32 GiB value and treats the heap as its own term.

gaps.question: Is the heap rule a fit or a measurement?
gaps.why: Four points: two heap sizes, two thread counts, six fleets. The live set after collection is read from the GC logs at three fleets and from the JMX gauge at the others. The per-device and per-thread coefficients are a fit to those points and are marked as estimates wherever they appear.

gaps.question: Is every knee one window?
gaps.why: Each rung of each search is one 15-minute window, three cycles, with no repetition; the two uncompressed baselines of the compression trials agree on CPU per collection to three decimals, which is the only repeat the campaign has. The rule's agreement with eight knees to within one rung is the evidence, not any single window.
